Beginner.learningGoal: Read and fix nullable warnings: ?, null checks, ?. and ??.
gotchas: The ! operator silences warnings without making anything safe
string? vs string in method signatures changes what callers must handle
?? and ??= evaluate the right side only when needed
goodSolutionShows: No ! used to hide real nulls
Signatures that say what can be null
Early returns or guard clauses for null
shapeHints: formatting a display name from optional first/last name
looking up a user's manager that may not exist

Intermediate.learningGoal: Use nullable attributes to describe APIs precisely.
gotchas: TryGet pattern needs [NotNullWhen(true)] for callers to get flow analysis
[MaybeNullWhen(false)] on out parameters of generic types
Nullable annotations are compile-time only: public APIs still need runtime checks
goodSolutionShows: Callers that compile without warnings and without !
shapeHints: a TryParse for a tenant code

Advanced.learningGoal: Migrate a small legacy API to nullable-aware code without breaking callers.
gotchas: Generic T? means different things for unconstrained, class and struct type parameters
Lazy initialisation patterns confuse flow analysis
Interfaces and implementations must agree on nullability
goodSolutionShows: Consistent annotations across interface and implementation
Correct use of T? with constraints
No warnings and no ! in the final code
